inputs.text:
Well, folks, once again we see the heavy hand of government welfare and state dependency being pushed on the hard-working public. Chief Minister M.K. Stalin has unveiled a manifesto that doubles women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 and hands out Rs 8,000 household coupons. Instead of encouraging traditional family values, personal responsibility, and the dignity of earned work, this administration prefers to expand the welfare state and foster a culture of handouts. 

They talk about targeting labor and redistributive measures for vulnerable groups, but all this does is undermine self-reliance and weaken the foundational role of the traditional household. On top of this wealth redistribution, they are offering free motor pumpsets to farmers and enhancing support for fishermen, while paying lip service to capitalist FDI growth and technocratic AI development. When the state gets this involved in picking economic winners and losers, it erodes traditional authority and fosters a dependency mindset that harms the very social fabric we rely on. True community strength comes from hard work and traditional values, not from government checks and socialist engineering.
